parsed.why: No trans criminalisation, no documented targeting, rare discrimination, no reported abuses — but also no acceptance record, near-zero visibility, no protections, conservative society; thin positives and thin negatives.

Gender nonconformity itself criminal under uncodified sharia; documented arrests, mass lashings, custody death, death penalty available, enforcement reaching travellers; welcome messaging cannot offset state criminal exposure.

Same-sex conduct legal, no trans offence, one region with third-gender acceptance; but strong public opposition, blocked protections, no hate-crime recognition, unresolved border-document questions, thin recourse.

Decriminalisation and pro-trans court rulings, unimpeded pride, drop-in centre, media and health non-discrimination rules; tempered by contested implementation, hostile politics, immoral-practices PDA exposure and repealed foreign-marriage recognition.

Active sodomy statute upheld, routine police pretext detention and extortion of gender-nonconforming people, custody abuse and document refusal — patterned state-facing exposure, partly offset by courts ruling for trans people.
